Tight and sensitive sites

Hand demolition, where a machine cannot be trusted

Demolition carried out by hand rather than by machine: tight sites with no access, internal walls and strip outs, renovation work, and structures hard against a neighbouring building. Slower by design, because the point is control rather than speed. Send photographs of the access and what has to come apart, and we will quote the labour and the method.

0456 220 552

Carried out under demolition licence AD214737

Before anything starts

Six things have to be settled first, and not all of them are ours

Most jobs that run late run late on this list rather than on the work itself. Each line says who owns it.

  1. 01

    Hazardous materials survey

    Who Max, through an accredited laboratory

    Internal work disturbs linings, ceilings and floor coverings, which is exactly where bonded asbestos sits in pre 1990 buildings.

  2. 02

    Structural advice on anything load bearing

    Who You, through an engineer

    Internal walls are not all partitions. Which ones are carrying load is the question that has to be answered before, not during.

  3. 03

    Approval or exemption

    Who You or your certifier

    Internal strip out in a tenancy, a heritage property or a strata building each have different requirements.

  4. 04

    Access and protection route

    Who Agreed between you and us

    How material gets out by hand: the path, the protection of floors and lifts, and the hours it can happen in.

  5. 05

    Service isolation

    Who You, with each authority or your trades

    Isolating what is in the walls being removed, without cutting what stays live.

  6. 06

    Dust, noise and neighbour management

    Who Max

    On an occupied building or a shared wall, this is in the contract rather than in the conversation.

The detail

When hand demolition is the right answer

  • There is no way in for a machine. A rear courtyard, a terrace with no side access, a basement, or an upper floor. If plant cannot get there, hands can.
  • The structure next door matters more. A party wall, a terrace in a row, or a building within a metre of the work. Vibration and reach are both risks a machine brings.
  • Only part of it is going. Internal walls out while the shell stays, which needs a cut line rather than a direction.
  • The building is occupied. Tenancies trading, or residents upstairs. Hours, noise, dust and the route material takes all become part of the method.
  • The material has to be recovered. Where joinery, brick, timber or fixtures are being kept, they come out intact rather than as rubble.
  • Heritage fabric is involved. Where what stays has to be protected to a standard, careful removal is the only method that meets it.

What we need to quote it

What has to be finished by when, and what is waiting on it

We attend the site before quoting anything substantial.

Internal work means asbestos in the linings

Ceilings, wall sheeting, wet area linings and vinyl floor tiles in pre 1990 buildings are all likely bonded asbestos. It is identified and removed under clearance before the hand work starts.

Before you book

What people ask about this one

Is hand demolition more expensive?
Per square metre, yes, and it is not close. What you are buying is control: the building next door intact, the floor above undamaged, and the part that stays unmarked. On the right job that is cheaper than the alternative.
Can you work in an occupied building?
Often, yes, with the hours, the access route, the dust control and the noise agreed first. What makes it work is planning the route material takes out, which is usually the constraint rather than the demolition itself.
Do you do strip outs for fit out?
Yes. Internal walls, ceilings, linings, floor coverings and fixtures removed back to whatever your builder needs: base building, shell, or a nominated line.
How do you know which walls are structural?
We do not assume, and nor should anyone. An engineer’s advice is what settles it, and on anything load bearing the propping goes in before the wall comes out.
Can material be salvaged?
Where it is worth keeping and the programme allows the extra time, yes. Brick, timber, joinery and fixtures all come out intact if that is in the scope. Say so before we start rather than after.
